messages:
cheng: heads up — support flagged a customer dashboard (acct: tenant-42) showing metrics that belong to tenant-77. looks like some prefetch/router affinity code incorrectly reuses a stale routing header when building telemetry keys.

samir: yikes. any repro steps?

cheng: open the console -> insights for tenant-42 (internal demo) and compare the top row ids with what we see for tenant-77 in prod. the ids in the quick-preview card match tenant-77. sanitized trace: `x-tenant-affinity: tenant-77` present in outgoing `internal-api/prefetch` call even though user session is tenant-42.

maria: that sounds like cross-tenant routing spill. could be the affinity middleware caching header per worker thread. did we recently change the router cache TTL?

aj: PR 4892 shortened affinity TTL and made the worker reuse header objects for perf. if that's the change, we have a hot path where header mutation + worker reuse causes bleed.

ops-bot: incident-created: INC-2026-042 - Console insights showing cross-tenant rows (high). Assigned to eng-platform.

samir: immediate mitigation: flip router to strict isolation mode (disable header pooling) and disable prefetch for insights cards by feature-flag. we should also snapshot which dashboards queried prefetched data in last 12h.

jen: can we remove the prefetched responses from cache store? I can script a purge by matching keys containing `prefetch:insights:` and tenant ids other than the requestor.

maria: do that. also coordinate with trust/privacy — this is a data exposure risk. set retention purge window for affected keys.

aj: rolling a 1-line revert to stop header object reuse and turning off prefetch flag for insights. will canary immediately. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4899

cheng: note: routing policy chosen fuzzes in metadata (we add `x-tenant-hint` for routing + `x-tenant-affinity` for telemetry). I think telemetry pipeline used affinity header as authoritative when attributing events; we need to attribute from session auth instead.

ops-bot: deploy-started: canary/console/2026-04-21T18:02:12Z by aj

samir: parallel ticket: sweep analytics indices that may have ingested mis-attributed rows. we need a map of event->tenant attribution for last 48h.

jen: purge script started against cache-store node-a. progress: 320 keys matched, 120 keys removed (some are in use).

maria: good. remind support to suspend any customer-facing share links until we confirm no more leakage.

aj: canary passed health checks. stable rollout in 20m unless any regressions.

cheng: longer term: add unit checks that header pooling cannot mutate per-request headers, and add a telemetry pre-attribute guard that refuses to attribute events based on `x-tenant-affinity` unless it matches authenticated session id.

samir: agreed. note for postmortem: root cause is worker-scoped header pooling combined with affinity header being used in analytics attribution. fixes: code revert, cache purge, analytics rebatch, and pre-merge guard.

maria: owners: aj (revert + deploy), jen (cache purge + verification), cheng (tests + telemetry guard), samir (analytics sweep + privacy). I'll post an update to #incidents and loop in legal.

ops-bot: deploy-complete: canary/console/2026-04-21T18:06:42Z - success

cheng: sanity check done: re-run same query flow — prefetch call now has `x-tenant-affinity` matching session (tenant-42). quickpreview cards show tenant-42 rows.

maria: thanks team. we'll follow up with postmortem and a telemetry attribution RFC. :thumbsup:
